elements.text: The math verifier — how it works
MathEquivalenceVerifier: a pure-C++ port of HF math-verify that turns a model's answer into a 0/1 reward for GRPO

Read from RL/src/reward/verifiers/MathEquivalenceVerifier.cpp (1671 lines, source as of 11-05 16:57), its tests, docs and parity data. Boxes with a page number jump there (click in view mode, Ctrl+click while editing).

1 · extract()
last \boxed{} → "final answer is" → "answer:" → $…$ → short answer-like tail → last number

6 · sym_equal()
exact · expand · decimals exact · 7 probes

On a RewardLoopWorker thread, once per rollout
VerifierRegistry maps type "math" → one shared MathEquivalenceVerifier; reward.verifiers maps each data_source to a type. RolloutWorker::agent_loop_postprocess decodes the response and queues it; the reward thread scores it. The 0/1 score is written to rm_scores[R−1] (the last response token); extra_info carries acc, pred (raw extracted answer) and method; since 11-05 the method is also written to each line of rollouts_<pid>.jsonl.

Built with SymEngine + GMP only
SymEngine has no LaTeX parser, so the file has its own recursive-descent parser that builds SymEngine objects; SymEngine supplies canonical form, expand, substitution and numeric evaluation. Static libsymengine (WITH_SYMENGINE_THREAD_SAFE=ON). make math_verifier_cli builds a JSONL CLI with no CUDA or Ray.

↗ Part of "BluTrain reward verifiers, explained" — open its overview
extract(): find the one string in a long chain-of-thought that is the model's answer
An unterminated <think> is left as is. Everything before the last </think> — including any \boxed{} in the reasoning — is ignored.
Six strategies — the first hit wins

1. last \boxed{…} or \fbox{…}
the later of the two; brace-matched; "\boxed 5" (space form) reads to the next $ or newline. Unbalanced braces → no box.

2. after the last "final answer is"
to end of line or "i hope"; strips leading : and *, trailing . and *

3. after the last "answer:"
same rules; also catches "Final Answer:"

4. last $…$ pair
content between the last two unescaped $ (\$5 is money, not math) — only if non-empty

5. the whole tail, if ≤ 64 chars and it reads like an answer
reads_like_answer: at most one word of 3+ letters that isn't a command or math word (sqrt, sin, log, and, …)

6. last number
scan back to the last digit, extend over [0-9.,] and a leading −

gt_answer(): if the ground truth contains \boxed / \fbox, take the last boxed content; otherwise the trimmed string as is. It then goes through the same normalize() as the prediction. ground_truth_parses(gt) is exposed so data can be filtered for ground truths the parser can't read.
a sentence ("answer" is a 3+ letter word) → last-number rule (fixed 11-05)
$$ leaves nothing between the last two $; the tail reads like an answer → mismatch

normalize(): the same rewrite for prediction and ground truth, so "\dfrac{1}{2}\text{ cm}" and "\frac12" can meet

1. protect \\
matrix row breaks → \x01 so the "\ " and "\," rules can't eat them

2. literal replacements
the kReplace table — delimiters, spacing, degrees, $, \dfrac, \%, unicode math and Greek

4. strip_text_blocks
unwrap a whole-answer \text{}/\textbf{}/\mathrm{}…; \mathrm{ → {; delete every remaining \text{…}

6. strip_unit_words
drop a trailing unit word after a space, digit or } — 26 words

spacing
\negthinspace … \thickspace → space (before \! and \ne on purpose) · \! removed · \, \; \: \quad \qquad "\ " → space

unicode Greek
α β γ δ θ λ μ σ φ ω Δ → \alpha … \Delta

Not done here: thousands separators (shape_of strips "1,000,000" later), \frac12 → \frac{1}{2} (the parser's single-token arg), 0.5 → \frac12 (unneeded: decimals parse exactly), lowercasing (the parser does it).
answers_equal(): decide what kind of answer this is before comparing its parts
First: drop a naming left-hand side

strip_named_lhs — if one side is lhs = rhs with one top-level "=" and the lhs just names something (x, x_1, YP, \tan Q, f(x), x'), and the other side has no relation, keep only the rhs. \in maps to "=", so x \in [1,2] becomes [1,2].
\begin{[pbBvV]matrix|array} … rows on \\, columns on &  → tag M (V for vmatrix)
≥ 2 items → tuple / interval; open and close brackets recorded

Must match first: ordered/unordered, open bracket, close bracket, item count (≤ 20, kMaxItems). Otherwise → NotEqual.
Ordered → pairwise answers_equal, first non-Equal wins.
Unordered → greedy O(n²) matching; leftovers → Unparsed if any comparison was Unparsed, else NotEqual.
expand_pm — an element with exactly one \pm or \mp (not \pmod) becomes two: a+b and a−b. More than one is left alone and the parser refuses it.

element_equal() and expr_equal(): equations, inequalities, ratios, percentages and multiple choice
take_approx: a \approx b → b if a is a name, else a.  x ≈ 3.14 → 3.14;  \pi \approx 3.14 → \pi.

same parts + operators,
in order or mirrored (flip)
Different numbers of operators → NotEqual. flip mirrors < ↔ >, <= ↔ >=, sub ↔ sup; notin has no mirror. Relation sides go back through answers_equal, so intervals and sets work there too.
equation_equal — the same line written differently

d1 = l1 − r1        d2 = l2 − r2

Equal  if  expand(d1 − d2) == 0          // same equation
       or  expand(d1 + d2) == 0          // sides swapped
       or  proportional(d1, d2)          // scaled

proportional: at all 9 probe points d1/d2 is one constant
nonzero ratio (rtol 1e-4), with ≥ 3 valid points;
points with |d2| < 1e-12 are skipped
d1 = 10x − 2y − 55, d2 = 20x − 4y − 110 = 2·d1 → the ratio is ½ at every point → proportional → sym, score 1 (verified). Likewise x > 3 vs 3 < x matches by mirroring.
parse_answer each side → SymEngine (page 5); a lone ":" that isn't a clock time is a ratio a/b
either side has % → remove every %, retry sym_equal
Multiple choice — only when the ground truth is a choice

choice_of:  \s*\{?\s*(?:\(([A-E])\)|([A-E])(?:[.:)]|$))\s*\}?\s*([\s\S]*)
            → {letter, rest}      (upper-case A–E only)

same letter    → Equal if either value is empty, or values not NotEqual
pred no letter → compare pred with the option's value  ("24" vs "B) 24")
otherwise      → NotEqual
Note: an unparsed value with the right letter still counts as Equal ("not NotEqual").

A hand-written recursive-descent parser for math-verify's LaTeX grammar, building SymEngine expressions directly

\cdot \times → *, \div \over → /, ** → ^. \boxed, \fbox and \phantom are skipped (their braces become a plain group). Accents (\overline → bar, \vec, \hat, …) make one Letter "acc{arg}". \operatorname{f} must be a known function. Any other command — \pm, \le, \begin, \int, \lim — throws Refuse (those are handled above the parser, or not at all).
NUM | LETTER ('_' sub)? | \pi | (expr) | |expr| | \frac arg arg | \sqrt[n] arg | func …

2x: implicit multiplication (next token is a Letter). 3\frac12: a lone integer followed by a \frac in (0,1) is a mixed number, ADDED (= 7/2), not multiplied. 2\frac{\pi}{3} stays a product. Numbers become exact GMP rationals: 0.25 is 1/4, never a float.

e and i
lone e = Euler's number, lone i/I = √−1 (not when subscripted)

\binom
exact for integers, else Γ form (so probing works)

\sum, \prod
integer bounds, range ≤ 1000, evaluated by substitution
Guards — cost is bounded by structure, not by a timer
characters per piece handed to the parser (was 256 until 11-05 16:57)
|n| in a^n for numeric a (and 1.2E… exponents)
|n| in x^n for symbolic x — re-checked after canonicalization
n! and min(k, n−k) for exact binomials
digits in one literal · elements in a set or tuple
size of an exact numeric power: (9^{10000})^{10000} is refused
expand() skipped above this many terms — (a+…+h)^50 has 2.6e8; probing decides instead
longer normalized answers: exact string match only (method too_long)

Refused → nullopt → "unparsed". Every refusal path (Refuse, and any SymEngine std::exception inside parse_expr) becomes nullopt, so an unreadable piece can only score through string equality. Examples: \foo{1}, x^{99999}, (9^{10000})^{10000}, 2|x| (Bar is not implicit), "2 3" (no implicit multiplication between numbers).

sym_equal(a, b): four ways two SymEngine expressions can be equal

1. se::eq(a, b)
structural equality after canonicalization — \sqrt{8} is already 2√2

2. expand(a − b) == 0
(x+1)^2 vs x^2+2x+1 — skipped if it would exceed kMaxExpandTerms = 5000 terms (probing decides)

3a. no free symbols, both exact rationals
both terminate (integers, 0.25, 6172.5) → must be identical. Otherwise exact_close: |a − b| ≤ 1e-4 · max(|a|, |b|) in exact arithmetic, never true at scale 0 (0 ≠ 4^-2016)

3b. no free symbols, an irrational side (π, √2, log)
complex doubles, both finite, no absolute tolerance: rtol 1e-4 if one side is a rounded decimal (3.1416 vs π), else 1e-9

4. free symbols → probe_equal
evaluate both at 7 fixed points; rtol 1e-9, or 1e-4 if a side contains a written decimal (2.58x); any disagreement → false; need ≥ 3 valid points
Any exception → false. Everything is deterministic: no RNG, no seed, no timer.
Fixed 11-05: before, rtol 1e-4 applied to exact integers too, so 20001 scored 1 against 20000 and 6172.5 against 6172.6. Now a tolerance is only used where an answer can legitimately be rounded.

γ ≈ 0.5772, the plastic number ≈ 1.3247, −1/√2, √5, −φ, plus two small values 0.0613 and −0.0419: awkward numbers unlikely to hit special values. Probe k gives symbol j the value kPoints[(k+j) % 7] + 0.1·j (equation proportionality also uses 17.31 and −29.7), so several symbols never get the same value. A point is skipped if either side is non-finite, both are 0, or evaluation throws; log of a negative goes complex instead of failing.
\sqrt{x^2} (orange) vs x (blue): equal at 3 probes, not at 2
At x = −0.7071 and −1.618 the sides give 0.7071 vs −0.7071 → any disagreement → mismatch, score 0 (verified). By contrast (x²−1)/(x−1) vs x+1 and sin²x + cos²x vs 1 agree at all 5 points → sym, 1.

New: metamorphic tests — no labels needed  (scripts/math_verifier_metamorphic.py)
For each ground truth (Dolci, Numina or a file), generate responses whose right score is known by construction, score them with math_verifier_cli, report the pass rate per transform.

positives — must score 1  (target ≥ 99%)
wrap_*: the answer inside 7 response endings (boxed, "final answer is", Answer:, **Final Answer:**, after </think>, before <|endoftext|>, a long preamble)
string rewrites: spaces, dfrac, left_right, named_lhs, reorder_set, eq_swap, eq_scale, ineq_mirror
SymPy rewrites: sympy_latex, sympy_expand, sympy_str · decimal: 7 significant digits of a non-terminating value

negatives — must score 0  (target 100%)
through SymPy: plus_one, negate, double, times_ten, rename_var
string: coarse_decimal (2 significant digits), swap_tuple, flip_bracket, drop_element, flip_inequality

properties  (0 violations)
reflexive: the ground truth against itself (= wrap_boxed)
symmetric: score(\boxed{a}, b) == score(\boxed{b}, a) for every bare-answer pair

SymPy-made pairs are kept only when SymPy and math-verify both agree with the intended label, so a failure points at this verifier rather than at the generator. Failures go to a file for reading. No results are saved in the repo yet.
What the 11-05 fixes closed, what is still open, performance, and where everything lives
rtol 1e-4 applied to exact integers — fixed: terminating decimals must be identical
letters are commuting symbols: d·o·g = g·o·d — still open
same letter + unparsable value counts as Equal — still open
Also: plain words like pi, sin, cos, exp, ln are matched inside longer words (spin, cost, expect). A ground truth that is literally "B" or "E" (a point name) is read as a multiple-choice letter.

Wiring — in code; no run config yet
VerifierRegistry registers type: math; RewardLoopWorker threads score it; RolloutWorker::write_trajectory logs each reward's method to rollouts_<pid>.jsonl. Still: no YAML in the repo uses type: math, and grpo_rlvr.yaml says math_equivalence, which RolloutWorker rejects; RLConfig.h / VerifierRegistry document that old name.

Short answers — fixed
"The answer is 5" now scores 1: a short tail is taken whole only if it reads like an answer, so a sentence reaches the last-number rule.

Escaping exceptions — fixed
score() now catches everything → method error, reward 0, instead of failing the session and evicting the prompt group.

Stale docs
The MATH_VERIFIER_*.md docs weren't updated on 11-05: PARSER_STATUS / DESIGN_OPTIONS still say items 1-4 are "not yet built", and the parity percentages predate the grammar port. Comments: "random-point probing" (points are fixed); x^23 "refused" (it parses).

Fast: about 68 µs per scoring on the 16:57 build (12,200 calls of a 61-case mix in 0.83 s, including JSON I/O and the heavy guard cases). Huge inputs are cut early: 4000-char tail, 1024-char pieces, 1024-char comparisons, kMaxExpandTerms before expand().

One instance per dataset is shared by all session threads. score() keeps no state; tables and regexes are function-local statics; a Parser is built per call. Relies on SymEngine built with WITH_SYMENGINE_THREAD_SAFE=ON (set by the Makefile's build step, not checkable from the repo). No timeouts: the guards on page 5 bound the work.
